name: Graphical User Interface
summary: Adversaries may attempt to gain access to a machine via a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to enhance execution capabilities. Access to a GUI allows a user to interact with a computer in a more visual manner than a CLI. A GUI allows users to move a cursor and click on interface objects, with a mouse and keyboard as the main input devices, as opposed to just using the keyboard. If physical access is not an option, then access might be possible via…

analytics.name: Analytic 1904
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an interactive desktop session Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), Virtual Network Computing (VNC), or vendor remote console to an Human-Machine Interface (HMI) or engineering station from a source Internet Protocol (IP) addresses outside the approved Network Management System (NMS) Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) subnet, or from an account not in the approved operator/engineer list, where the session subsequently interacts with Industrial Control System (ICS) control elements. analytics.name: Analytic 2144
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies Secure Shell (SSH) sessions with X11 forwarding or Virtual Network Computing (VNC) connections to Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux hosts from unexpected source Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, combined with X11 application launches from the session. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

analytics.name: Analytic 2197
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies remote console or web management sessions to Industrial Control System (ICS) network devices from IP addresses that are not approved Network Management System (NMS) hosts, where the sessions access device configuration interfaces. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.
